title: Shopinbos vs Bumpa
h1: Shopinbos vs Bumpa for Nigerian sellers
sub: Bumpa is a well-known Nigerian app for running a small business, from stock to sales records. Shopinbos focuses on selling online: an AI-built store, pay on delivery with riders, and supplier stock you can sell. Here’s an honest look at which fits you.
us: You want Rex to build your store from a chat
Your customers want pay on delivery with riders
You want to sell supplier products without buying stock
You want an AI assistant that replies in English and Pidgin
them: You run a physical shop and record walk-in sales
You want detailed sales and bookkeeping records
You already use Bumpa and it works for you
You prefer a tool many Nigerian sellers already know
rows: Price | Free plan for up to 20 products, then from ₦6,000 a month | Subscription plans, check Bumpa’s pricing page for current prices | tie
Store setup | Rex builds your store from a chat in about 5 minutes | Website builder with ready-made designs | us
Walk-in and offline sales | Built mainly for selling online | Known for recording shop and online sales in one place | them
Business records and reports | Orders, stock and simple numbers | A strong focus on records, stock and reports | them
Pay on delivery | Built in for orders up to ₦50,000 in four cities, with rider codes and same-day cash | Check how Bumpa handles pay on delivery and cash collection | us
Riders and delivery | Book riders from the order, delivery price shown at checkout | Delivery options available, check which partners and cities | tie
Find stock to sell | Checked Nigerian suppliers, dropship or wholesale | Built around managing your own stock | us
Customer chats | Peggy answers customer chats in English and Pidgin | Tools for social selling and customer records, check their current AI features | us
Track record | Newer, built for selling online in Nigeria | Used by Nigerian small businesses for years | them
steps: Download or copy your product list from Bumpa into a spreadsheet
Upload it in Shopinbos, Rex maps the fields
Point your domain to Shopinbos or use yourname.shopinbos.com
Turn on pay on delivery and riders
kws: best app for small business in Nigeria
faq: Is Bumpa good for Nigerian businesses? | Yes, many Nigerian small businesses use Bumpa, especially to keep records of stock and sales. If you mainly sell online and want pay on delivery with riders built in, compare both before you choose.
Can I move from Bumpa to Shopinbos? | Yes. Put your products in a spreadsheet, upload it, and Rex maps the fields. You can also start fresh by telling Rex what you sell.

Is Shopinbos cheaper than Bumpa? | Shopinbos has a free plan for up to 20 products, and paid plans from ₦6,000 a month. Check Bumpa’s pricing page for their current plans and compare what each one includes.

title: Shopinbos vs Selar
h1: Shopinbos vs Selar for Nigerian sellers
sub: Selar is popular with creators selling ebooks, courses and other digital products. Shopinbos is built for physical products sold in Nigeria, with pay on delivery, riders and selling on WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok. Here’s how they compare.
us: You sell physical products like fashion, beauty or gadgets
Your customers want pay on delivery
You need riders and delivery prices at checkout
You want to find supplier stock to sell
them: You sell ebooks, courses, templates or other digital products
You have buyers outside Nigeria paying in other currencies
You want affiliates to promote your products
You only need a simple checkout link for a few items
rows: Best for | Physical products sold in Nigeria | Digital products, courses and creators | tie
Price | Free plan, then from ₦6,000 a month | Free to start, with a fee taken from sales, check Selar’s pricing page | tie
Digital products and courses | Not our main focus | Built for it, with instant delivery of files | them
Selling abroad | Nigeria first | Accepts payments in several currencies | them
Pay on delivery | Built in, with 4-digit rider codes and same-day cash | Built mainly for paying upfront | us
Delivery | Riders booked from the order, interstate through partner companies | You arrange delivery of physical items yourself | us
Find stock to sell | Checked Nigerian suppliers, dropship or wholesale | Not offered as a main feature | us
Selling on WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok | One product list and one inbox for all channels | Share your product links on any channel | us
Store and domain | Store at yourname.shopinbos.com, your own domain on paid plans | Store page for your products, check their current domain options | tie
steps: List the physical products you sell on Selar
Tell Rex what you sell, or upload a spreadsheet
Share your new store link on WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok
Turn on pay on delivery and riders
kws: best platform to sell online in Nigeria
faq: Can I use Selar and Shopinbos together? | Yes. Some sellers keep digital products such as ebooks or courses on Selar and run their physical products on Shopinbos. Use each for what it does best.
Is Selar good for physical products? | You can list physical products on Selar, but you arrange delivery yourself. If your buyers want pay on delivery and riders, Shopinbos has these built in.
How much does Selar charge? | Selar is free to start and takes a fee from sales. Fees change, so check Selar’s pricing page for the current numbers.

title: Shopinbos vs Wix

us: You mainly want to sell products in Nigeria
You want to pay for your plan in naira
Your customers want pay on delivery
You run your shop from your phone
them: You want full control over how every page looks
You need a blog, bookings or portfolio as well as a shop
You sell to customers in many countries
You already have a Wix site you are happy with
rows: Price | Free plan, then from ₦6,000 a month, in naira | Selling online needs a paid plan, usually priced in US dollars, check Wix’s pricing page | us
Payments in Nigeria | Cards, transfer and USSD built in, through Paystack | Check which payment providers Wix supports in Nigeria | us
Pay on delivery | Built in, with rider codes and same-day cash | Manual offline payment options | us
Local riders at checkout | Built in for Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan and Port Harcourt | Shipping settings, you arrange local delivery | us
Design freedom | Templates and settings | Drag-and-drop editor with hundreds of templates | them
More than a shop | Focused on selling | Blogs, bookings, portfolios and more | them
AI help | Rex builds your store, Peggy answers chats in English and Pidgin | AI tools to help build your site | tie
Selling on WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok | One product list and one inbox | Social tools and integrations, check what works in Nigeria | us
Selling worldwide | Nigeria first | Strong, in many countries | them
steps: Export your products from Wix as a CSV
Upload it in Shopinbos, Rex maps the fields
Point your domain to Shopinbos
Turn on Paystack payments, pay on delivery and riders
kws: website builder for selling in Nigeria
faq: Can I use Wix in Nigeria? | Yes. You can build a Wix site from Nigeria. Before you choose it for a shop, check how you will take payments in naira and how you will arrange delivery.
Is Wix better than Shopinbos for design? | If you want to control every detail of every page, Wix gives you more freedom. Shopinbos gives you ready templates so you can start selling quickly.
Can I keep my domain if I move from Wix? | Yes, on a Shopinbos paid plan you can connect your own domain. Check your domain settings with whoever you registered it with.

them: You sell only a handful of products

You don’t want any monthly plan
Your customers always pay before you deliver

faq: Does Shopinbos use Paystack? | Yes. Payments on Shopinbos go through Paystack, so customers can pay by card, bank transfer or USSD. The fee is 1.5% + ₦100, with the ₦100 waived under ₦2,500, capped at ₦2,000.
Is Paystack Storefront free? | Paystack Storefront has no separate plan to pay for, and Paystack’s transaction fees apply. Check Paystack’s pricing page for the current fees.

When should I move from Storefront to Shopinbos? | Many sellers move when they want pay on delivery, riders, more products or one inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok. If a simple payment page still works for you, there’s no rush.

title: Shopinbos vs selling on Jumia
h1: Selling on Jumia vs your own Shopinbos store
sub: Jumia is one of the best-known online marketplaces in Nigeria, with shoppers already on it. Your own Shopinbos store gives you your own brand, your own prices and your own customers. Many sellers do both. Here’s an honest look at each.
us: You want to keep your own list of customers
You want your own brand, not a listing beside other sellers
You sell through WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok
You want buyers to come back and order from you directly
them: You want shoppers who are already searching for products
You don’t have a following on social media yet
You want delivery handled across Nigeria by the marketplace
You sell branded items people search for by name
rows: Cost | Free plan, then from ₦6,000 a month, plus payment fees | Commission on each sale and other seller fees, check Jumia’s seller pages | tie
Ready shoppers | You bring your own buyers from WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok and Google | A large number of shoppers already browse the site | them
Buyer trust | You build it with reviews, Status and good service | A well-known name many buyers already trust | them
Delivery reach | Riders in Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan and Port Harcourt, interstate through partner companies | Jumia’s own delivery network across Nigeria | them
Your customers | Your customer list, your chats, your follow-ups | Buyers order from Jumia, contact goes through Jumia | us
Your brand | Your own store, name and domain | Your shop sits beside other sellers of similar items | us
Pricing | You set prices, discounts and bundles | You set prices, next to competing listings on the same page | us
Selling on social media | One product list and one inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok | Built for selling on the marketplace | us
Payouts | Paid to your bank every Friday, withdraw early any time | Paid on Jumia’s schedule, check their seller terms | tie

own online store vs marketplace Nigeria
faq: Can I sell on Jumia and Shopinbos at the same time? | Yes. Many sellers use a marketplace to reach new shoppers and their own store for customers who come back. Check Jumia’s seller rules about contacting their buyers outside the platform.
How much does Jumia charge sellers? | Jumia charges a commission on sales and may charge other fees, which vary by category. Check Jumia’s seller pages for the current numbers.

Why have my own store if I’m already on Jumia? | Your own store lets you keep your customers, set your own prices without a competitor beside you, and sell on WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok from one place.

title: Shopinbos vs selling only on Instagram

us: You are losing orders in busy DMs
You want buyers to pay without long back-and-forth
Your customers want pay on delivery with riders
You want a backup if your Instagram account has trouble
them: You are still testing if a product will sell

You enjoy handling every sale by chat
You don’t want another app yet

kws: do I need a website if I sell on Instagram
faq: Do I need a store if I already sell on Instagram? | Not on day one. But a store lets buyers order and pay without waiting for your reply, and keeps your shop safe if your account has trouble.
Can I still sell on Instagram with Shopinbos? | Yes. Shopinbos helps you sell on Instagram, WhatsApp, TikTok and your own store, with one product list and one inbox.

What happens if my Instagram account is hacked? | If Instagram is your only shop, you can lose your followers and your orders at once. With your own store, your products and customer list stay with you.
